key_insight: Fed-GRPO turns the reward signals already produced by GRPO into a privacy-preserving federated training loop that improves reasoning without sharing raw data.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to train large reasoning models across silos under privacy or regulatory constraints while cutting communication costs dramatically.
method: Signal-weighted aggregation: clients with higher reward variability get more influence during model aggregation.
Global reward calibration: per-prompt objectives are adjusted using the gap between local and global rewards.
Adaptive sparse communication: bandwidth is allocated to the most informative client updates.
evidence_signal: On mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the method outperforms other federated baselines, approaches centralized training, and achieves up to 32× communication reduction with reported compression as high as 621×.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and stability of reward statistics, so noisy or weak reward signals could make aggregation and sparse communication less reliable.
paper_title: Fed-GRPO: Reward-Signal-Driven Federated Group Relative Policy Optimization
